title: Release rules for a software team

blocks.text: A software team (not GridCap) picks which features ship in the next release. The product owner's rules come in four kinds, each a list of tuples of feature names:

items: `excludes`: `(a, b)`, "a and b never ship in the same release";
`needs_one_of`: `(a, [o1, o2, ...])`, "a needs at least one of the options";
`bundles`: `(a, b)`, "a and b ship together or not at all".

blocks.text: `x[f]` is the Boolean "feature f ships". In logic, the four kinds are

Write `add_rules(model, x, requires, excludes, needs_one_of, bundles)` in `release.py`: one CP-SAT constraint per rule, with no linear algebra and no big-M. The tests fix which features ship and ask CP-SAT whether the rules allow it. About eight lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from release import add_rules

features = ["login", "billing", "invoices", "email", "sms", "beta_ui", "classic_ui", "api", "sdk"]
rules = dict(requires=[("billing", "login")], excludes=[("beta_ui", "classic_ui")],
             needs_one_of=[("invoices", ["email", "sms"])], bundles=[("api", "sdk")])


def check(plan):
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    x = {f: model.new_bool_var(f) for f in features}
    add_rules(model, x, **rules)
    for f, var in x.items():
        model.add(var == (1 if f in plan else 0))
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = 5
    return solver.status_name(solver.solve(model))


for plan in ({"billing", "login"}, {"billing"}, {"beta_ui", "classic_ui"}, {"invoices"},
             {"invoices", "sms"}, {"api"}, {"api", "sdk"}):
    print("plan", sorted(plan), "->", check(plan))

cases.says: a feature ships with the feature it requires, and is refused without it
one of two excluded features may ship, and both together are refused
a feature that needs one of several options ships with one, and is refused with none
a bundle ships with both features, and either one alone is refused
the required feature may ship on its own
a feature that needs one of several options may ship with more than one

origin.section: GridCap's Rules Become One Constraint Each, With No Big-M

concepts: requirement, exclusion, needs-one-of and all-or-nothing rules are one logic constraint each
bool_or, bool_and, implication, at-most-one, exactly-one and equality each allow a fixed truth table
